text.en: Find the notes of line 1: each one waits until you're on it.
text.es: Busca las notas de la frase 1: cada una te espera hasta que estés en ella.

text.en: The Union Haggadah prints it as a solo verse and a chorus: one singer leads each verse, and everyone answers "Lecha ulecha", yours and yours.

source.en: The Union Haggadah (Central Conference of American Rabbis, 1923), pp. 84 and 85, read from the scan

text.en: Now lines 1 and 2 joined: hear them, then sing them back.

Now lines 20 to 23 joined: hear them, then sing them back.

text.en: Line 24 is line 8 again. Sing it with the guide.
Hear line 25, then sing it back.
Now lines 24 and 25 joined: hear them, then sing them back.
Ki lo nae start to end, with the guide.
Adir bimlucha start to end, with the guide.
Kadosh bimlucha start to end, with the guide.
Takif bimlucha start to end, with the guide.
The whole song, with the guide.
text.es: La canción entera, con la guía.

text.en: Sing your part with the other parts, and the guide with you. Hold your line while the others move.
text.es: Canta tu parte con las demás voces, y la guía contigo. Mantente firme en ella mientras las otras se mueven.

text.en: The guide drops out: your part with the others only. Give me my note plays your first note quietly.
text.es: La guía deja de cantar: tu parte, solo con las demás voces. "Escuchar mi nota" te da tu primera nota, suave.

text.en: Once more on your own, from the top.
text.es: Otra vez sin guía, desde el principio.

text.en: Record the tune of Ki Lo Na'eh in Sing, with the other parts playing.
It was already in the book's first edition of 1908, with the same tune in the same key, though with only its first verse.

source.en: The Union Haggadah (Central Conference of American Rabbis, 1908), pp. 54 and 55, read from the scan
